verses.zh: 大卫又聚集以色列中所有挑选的人三万。
verses.en: David again assembled[NOTE:1] all the best[NOTE:2] men in Israel, 30,000 in number.
notes: The translation understands the verb to be a defective spelling of וַיֶּאֱסֹף (vayyeʾesof) due to quiescence of the letter א (alef). The root therefore is אָסַף (ʾasaf, “to gather”). The Masoretes, however, pointed the verb as וַיֹּסֶף (vayyosef), understanding it to be a form of יָסַף (yasaf, “to add”). This does not fit the context, which calls for a verb of gathering.
Or “chosen.”
verses.commentary: 6:1 "all the chosen men" This was an especially chosen group of warriors (cf. 1 Sam. 26:2).

verses.zh: 大卫起身，率领跟随他的众人前往，要从巴拉・犹大将　神的约柜运来；这约柜就是坐在二基路伯上万军之耶和华留名的约柜。
verses.en: David and all the men who were with him traveled[NOTE:1] to[NOTE:2] Baalah[NOTE:3] in Judah to bring up from there the ark of God which is called by the name[NOTE:4] of the Lord of Heaven’s Armies, who sits enthroned between the cherubim that are on it.
notes: Heb “arose and went.”
Heb “from,” but the following context indicates they traveled to this location.
This is another name for Kiriath Jearim (see 1 Chr 13:6).

The MT has here a double reference to the name (שֵׁם שֵׁם, shem shem). Many medieval Hebrew mss in the first occurrence point the word differently and read the adverb שָׁם (sham, “there”). This is also the understanding of the Syriac Peshitta (Syr., taman). While this yields an acceptable understanding to the text, it is more likely that the MT reading results from dittography. If the word did occur twice, one might have expected the first occurrence to have the article. The present translation therefore reads שֵׁם only once.
verses.commentary:
6:2

NASB, NKJV, NRSV
"Baale-judah"

TEV
"Baalah in Judah"

NJB
"Baalah of Judah

REB
"Baalath-judah"

JPSOA
"Baalim of Judah"

LXX
"rulers of Judah"

Peshitta
"men of Judah"

The JPSOA footnote says, "identical with Baalah, another name for Kiriath-jearim, where the Ark
had been kept (cf. 1 Sa. 6:21; 1 Chr. 13:6)." Kiriath-jearim was also called "Kiriath-baal" (cf. Josh. 15:9,60; 18:14).
Baalah is a FEMININE form and may have been a Canaanite name for Asherah, Astarte, Anath.

It is possible because of 1 Sam. 6:21, that "Baal" (see NIDOTTE, vol. 4, pp. 422-428) referred to
YHWH's ark being in Kiriath-jearim. The word "baal" means "owner," "master," "lord." Originally it did not denote the
male Canaanite fertility god and could be used of YHWH.

▣ "the ark" Notice how this sacred covenant box is named and characterized.

- of God (the Elohim, vv. 3,4,6,7; of YHWH, v. 9)

- called by the Name of YHWH of hosts

- who enthroned above the cherubim

Notice how "the Name" is emphasized (cf. Deut. 28:10; 1 Kgs. 8:43)

- capitalized in NASB

- called "the very name of YHWH of Hosts"

This awe and respect due to God's name is seen in the Ten Commandments, Exodus. 20:7; Lev. 19:12; 24:16.

verses.zh: 他们将　神的约柜从冈上亚比拿达的家里抬出来，放在新车上；亚比拿达的两个儿子乌撒和亚希约赶这新车。
verses.en: They loaded the ark of God on a new cart and carried it from the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill. Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, were guiding the new cart.
verses.commentary:
6:3 "they placed it on a new cart" This is exactly what the Philistines did when they returned the captured
ark (cf. 1 Sam. 6:7), but the Law of Moses demanded it be carried by Levites (cf. Num. 4:15; Deut. 10:8; 31:9,25,26;
1 Chr. 15:2).

Disobedience always caused problems (i.e., Uzzah's death, cf. 2 Sam. 6:6-8).

▣ "from the house of Abinadab" This is recorded in 1 Sam. 7:1-2.

verses.zh: 他们将　神的约柜从冈上亚比拿达家里抬出来的时候，亚希约在柜前行走。
verses.en: They brought[NOTE:1] it with the ark of God from the house of Abinadab on the hill. Ahio was walking in front of the ark,
notes: Heb “lifted.”

verses.zh: 大卫和以色列的全家在耶和华面前，用松木制造的各样乐器和琴、瑟、鼓、钹、锣，作乐跳舞。
verses.en: while David and all Israel[NOTE:1] were energetically celebrating before the Lord, singing[NOTE:2] and playing various stringed instruments,[NOTE:3] tambourines, rattles,[NOTE:4] and cymbals.
notes: Heb “all the house of Israel.”

Heb “were celebrating before the Lord with all woods of fir” (cf. KJV, ASV, NASB). If the text is retained, the last expression must be elliptical, referring to musical instruments made from fir wood. But it is preferable to emend the text in light of 1 Chr 13:8, which reads “were celebrating before the Lord with all strength and with songs.”
Heb “with zithers [?] and with harps.”
That is, “sistrums” (so NAB, NIV); ASV, NASB, NRSV, CEV, NLT “castanets.”
verses.commentary:
6:5 "all kinds of instruments" See notes at Psalm 150 online. Israelites were a musical people! JPSOA
footnote thinks this is a corrupt text and prefers the parallel in 1 Chr. 13:8, "with all their might and with songs" (i.e.,
LXX, DSS have this reading here).

verses.zh: 到了拿艮的禾场，因为牛失前蹄（或译：惊跳），乌撒就伸手扶住　神的约柜。
verses.en: When they arrived at the threshing floor of Nacon,[NOTE:1] Uzzah reached out and grabbed hold of[NOTE:2] the ark of God,[NOTE:3] because the oxen stumbled.
notes: 1 Chr 13:9 has “Kidon.”
Or “steadied.”
Heb “and Uzzah reached out toward the ark of God and grabbed it.”
verses.commentary:
6:6 "the threshing floor" Grain was placed in piles on hard grounded hills. Animals pulling heavy sleds were
dragged over the grain to loosen the husk from the kernel. Then men with wooden forks lifted the grain into the air so that
the wind would blow away the husks while the heavier grains fell back to earth.

Apparently the oxen veered aside to eat the grains and the new cart almost fell over.

verses.zh: 神耶和华向乌撒发怒，因这错误击杀他，他就死在　神的约柜旁。
verses.en: The Lord was so furious with Uzzah,[NOTE:1] he[NOTE:2] killed him on the spot[NOTE:3] for his negligence.[NOTE:4] He died right there beside the ark of God.
notes: Heb “and the anger of the Lord burned against Uzzah.”
Heb “God.”
Heb “there.” Since this same term occurs later in the verse it is translated “on the spot” here for stylistic reasons.
The phrase “his negligence” is absent from the LXX.
verses.commentary:
6:7 No one but Levites could touch (or for that matter, transport) the holy ark of the covenant
(cf. Deut. 10:8).

Remember that Deity is described in anthropomorphic language (i.e., anger); the only language
humans understand.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE USED TO DESCRIBE DEITY

▣

NASB, TEV
"his irreverence"

NKJV
"his error"

NJB
"this crime"

REV
"his imprudent action"

JPSOA, Targums
"his indiscretion"

LXX
—omit—

Peshitta
"he put forth his hand"

The MT has the NOUN (BDB 1016), which has an uncertain meaning.

- "error" comes from an Aramaic root

- the Peshitta's translation comes from the parallel in 1 Chr. 13:10

- "indiscretion" comes from the Aramaic Targums

- "careless" from Akkadian root (KB 1994, NET)

The UBS Text Project, p. 221, supports the MT with a "B" rating, against (NRSV, Peshitta).

verses.zh: 大卫因耶和华击杀（原文是闯杀）乌撒，心里愁烦，就称那地方为毗列斯・乌撒，直到今日。
verses.en: David was angry because the Lord attacked[NOTE:1] Uzzah; so he called that place Perez Uzzah,[NOTE:2] which remains its name to this very day.
notes: Heb “because the Lord broke out [with] a breaking out [i.e., an outburst] against Uzzah.”
The name Perez Uzzah means in Hebrew “the outburst [against] Uzzah.”
verses.commentary:
6:8

NASB
"the Lord's outburst"

NKJV
"the Lord's outbreak"

NRSV
"the Lord had burst forth with an outburst"

NJB
"YHWH's having broken out"

JPSOA
"the Lord had inflicted a breach"

LXX
"the Lord breached a breach"

Peshitta
"the Lord had stricken"

The MT has a VERB and NOUN from the same root.

- VERB ‒ BDB 829 I, KB 971, Qal PERFECT

- NOUN ‒ BDB 829

The LXX comes close to the literal phrase. BDB 829 I, #6, has "break out of YHWH in sudden outburst
of divine judgment." Some examples:

- Exod. 19:22,24 ‒ warning of judgment on Mt. Sinai

- 1 Chr. 14:11 ‒ God breaking out on David's enemies

- Ps. 60:3 ‒ defeat of Israel's army for sin

- Ps. 106:29 ‒ judgment because of Israel's sin at Baal-Peor, Num. 25:3

▣ "Perez-uzzah" This is a play on the VERB "break out" (see above). It literally means
"the break-through of Uzzah."

verses.zh: 那日，大卫惧怕耶和华，说：「耶和华的约柜怎可运到我这里来？」
verses.en: David was afraid of the Lord that day and said, “How will the ark of the Lord ever come to me?”
verses.commentary:
6:9 "David was afraid of the Lord that day" What a sad statement. The God who
had brought David such peace, power, and was constantly with him, was now an object of fear. Fear, not reverence,
brings emotional and physical separation.

David was truly human. His fear is overcome in this context by the divine prosperity of Obed-edom (vv. 11,12).

verses.zh: 于是大卫不肯将耶和华的约柜运进大卫的城，却运到迦特人俄别・以东的家中。
verses.en: So David was no longer willing to bring the ark of the Lord to be with him in the City of David. David left it in the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite.
verses.commentary:
6:10 "Obed-edom the Gittite" This is probably the Levite mentioned in 1 Chr. 15:18,21, a descendant of
Merarite. He is called a "Gittite" because he was from Gath (cf. Josh. 21:25).

verses.zh: 耶和华的约柜在迦特人俄别・以东家中三个月；耶和华赐福给俄别・以东和他的全家。
verses.en: The ark of the Lord remained in the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite for three months. The Lord blessed Obed-Edom and all his family.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “house,” both here and in v. 12.

verses.zh: 有人告诉大卫王说：「耶和华因为约柜赐福给俄别・以东的家和一切属他的。」大卫就去，欢欢喜喜地将　神的约柜从俄别・以东家中抬到大卫的城里。
verses.en: King David was told,[NOTE:1] “The Lord has blessed the family of Obed-Edom and everything he owns because of the ark of God.” So David went and joyfully brought the ark of God from the house of Obed-Edom to the City of David.
notes: Heb “and it was told to King David, saying.”

verses.zh: 抬耶和华约柜的人走了六步，大卫就献牛与肥羊为祭。
verses.en: Those who carried the ark of the Lord took six steps and then David[NOTE:1] sacrificed an ox and a fatling calf.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (David) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
verses.commentary:
6:13 David moves the ark by bearers (presumably Levites, cf. 1 Chr. 15:2). In addition he sacrificed along
the way (again presumably by priests). The word "paces" (BDB 857) may refer metaphorically to specific stations
along the way, not every six steps.

verses.zh: 大卫穿着细麻布的以弗得，在耶和华面前极力跳舞。
verses.en: Now David, wearing a linen ephod, was dancing with all his strength before the Lord.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and David was dancing with all his strength before the Lord, and David was girded with a linen ephod.”
verses.commentary:
6:14

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, TEV, NJB
"dancing"

JPSOA
"whirled"

LXX
"struck upon tuned instruments"

Peshitta
"sang praises"

The MT has the VERB (BDB 502, KB 500, Pilpel PARTICIPLE;
NIDOTTE, vol. 2, p. 228) which implies a circular motion with the added phrase, "with all his might." It was
a dancing outburst of joy!
His fear was over!

▣ "wearing an ephod" This was worn by priests. The LXX translates it as "a distinguishing garment."
See full note at 1 Chr. 15:27 online.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LINEN

SPECIAL TOPIC: EPHOD

verses.zh: 这样，大卫和以色列的全家欢呼吹角，将耶和华的约柜抬上来。
verses.en: David and all Israel[NOTE:1] were bringing up the ark of the Lord, shouting and blowing trumpets.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “all the house of Israel.” A few medieval Hebrew mss and the Syriac Peshitta lack the words “the house.”
Heb “the shofar” (the ram’s horn trumpet).
verses.commentary:
6:15 "shouting" Some scholars think this was their typical war cry but others, singing (v. 5).

▣ "the trumpet" This was the left ram's horn called a shophar (BDB 1051; NIDOTTE, vol. 4, pp. 68-69).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HORNS USED BY ISRAEL

verses.zh: 耶和华的约柜进了大卫城的时候，扫罗的女儿米甲从窗户里观看，见大卫王在耶和华面前踊跃跳舞，心里就轻视他。
verses.en: As the ark of the Lord entered the City of David, Saul’s daughter Michal looked out the window. When she saw King David leaping and dancing before the Lord, she despised him.[NOTE:1]
notes: The Hebrew text adds “in her heart.” Cf. CEV “she was disgusted (+ with him TEV)”; NLT “was filled with contempt for him”; NCV “she hated him.”
verses.commentary:
6:16 "leaping" This is a rare VERB (BDB 808 II, KB 921, Piel PARTICIPLE)
which denoted agility and here, excited dancing.

▣ "she despised him in her heart" One wonders how the love she once expressed to David
(cf. 1 Sam. 18:20,28; 19:11-17) had grown cold. Possibly it was her removal from her home with Paltiel (cf. 2 Sam. 3:13-16).

This outburst of anger against David meant they would never have children (cf. v, 23). She became
only a figurehead of Saul's family in David's harem.

verses.zh: 众人将耶和华的约柜请进去，安放在所预备的地方，就是在大卫所搭的帐幕里。大卫在耶和华面前献燔祭和平安祭。
verses.en: They brought the ark of the Lord and put it in its place[NOTE:1] in the middle of the tent that David had pitched for it. Then David offered burnt sacrifices and peace offerings before the Lord.
notes: The Syriac Peshitta lacks “in its place.”
verses.commentary:
6:17 "the tent which David had pitched for it" This implies the tabernacle of the wilderness was no longer
in existence. It was made of animal skin and fiber. It deteriorated over time. David made a new tent (cf. 1 Chr. 15:1).
See full note online at 1 Chr. 15:1.

SPECIAL TOPIC: TABERNACLE OF THE WILDERNESS

▣ "burnt offerings" Often sacrifices were offered in a series (cf. Leviticus 1-7).

SPECIAL TOPIC: BURNT OFFERING

▣ "peace offerings" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE OFFERING.

verses.zh: 大卫献完了燔祭和平安祭，就奉万军之耶和华的名给民祝福，
verses.en: When David finished offering the burnt sacrifices and peace offerings, he pronounced a blessing over the people in the name of the Lord of Heaven’s Armies.
verses.commentary:
6:18 "he blessed the people in the name of the Lord of hosts" This is exactly
what Solomon later did at the dedication of the Temple (cf. 1 Kgs. 8:14-15).

SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord OF HOSTS

verses.zh: 并且分给以色列众人，无论男女，每人一个饼，一块肉，一个葡萄饼；众人就各回各家去了。
verses.en: He then handed out to each member of the entire assembly of Israel,[NOTE:1] both men and women, a portion of bread, a date cake,[NOTE:2] and a raisin cake. Then all the people went home.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “to all the people, to all the throng of Israel.”

The Hebrew word used here אֶשְׁפָּר (ʾespar) is found in the OT only here and in the parallel passage found in 1 Chr 16:3. Its exact meaning is uncertain, although the context indicates that it was a food of some sort (cf. KJV “a good piece of flesh”; NRSV “a portion of meat”). The translation adopted here (“date cake”) follows the lead of the Greek translations of the LXX, Aquila, and Symmachus (cf. NASB, NIV, NLT).
Heb “and all the people went, each to his house.”
verses.commentary:
6:19 "he distributed. . ." In this period worshipers were often given a food gift. Here

- cake of bread (BDB 319 CONSTRUCT BDB 530)

- cake of dates (BDB 80 and BDB 25)

- cake of raisins (BDB 84 and BDB 25)

These were given to all who attended the event, men and women. It was possibly part of the Peace Offering
concept of a communal meal eaten with YHWH. Eating together was a cultural event between friends!

The very helpful series of translator helps from UBS, called Handbook of. . .," p. 744,
gives a different possible translation for these worship gifts.

- loaves of bread

- cuts of meat (NKJV, NRSV, TEV, REB, Peshitta, Vulgate' Josephus, Antiq. 7.4.2, "with a portion of the sacrifice")

- some type of dessert

For me this better fits the concept of a shared meal (i.e., Peace Offerings).

verses.zh: 大卫回家要给眷属祝福；扫罗的女儿米甲出来迎接他，说：「以色列王今日在臣仆的婢女眼前露体，如同一个轻贱人无耻露体一样，有好大的荣耀啊！」
verses.en: When David went home to pronounce a blessing on his own house,[NOTE:1] Michal, Saul’s daughter, came out to meet him.[NOTE:2] She said, “How the king of Israel has distinguished[NOTE:3] himself this day! He has exposed himself today before his servants’ slave girls the way a vulgar fool[NOTE:4] might do!”
notes: Heb “and David returned to bless his house.”
Heb “David.” The name has been replaced by the pronoun (“him”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “honored.”
Heb “one of the foolish ones.”

verses.zh: 大卫对米甲说：「这是在耶和华面前；耶和华已拣选我，废了你父和你父的全家，立我作耶和华民以色列的君，所以我必在耶和华面前跳舞。
verses.en: David replied to Michal, “It was before the Lord! I was celebrating before the Lord, who chose me over your father and his entire family[NOTE:1] and appointed me as leader over the Lord’s people Israel.
notes: Heb “all his house”; CEV “anyone else in your family.”

verses.zh: 我也必更加卑微，自己看为轻贱。你所说的那些婢女，她们倒要尊敬我。」
verses.en: I am willing to shame and humiliate myself even more than this.[NOTE:1] But with the slave girls whom you mentioned, let me be distinguished.”
notes: Heb “and I will shame myself still more than this and I will be lowly in my eyes.”

verses.zh: 扫罗的女儿米甲，直到死日，没有生养儿女。
verses.en: Now Michal, Saul’s daughter, had no children to the day of her death.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 6:1-5

1Now David again gathered all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand. 2And
David arose and went with all the people who were with him to Baale-judah, to bring up from there the ark
of God which is called by the Name, the very name of the Lord of hosts
who is enthroned above the cherubim. 3They placed the ark of God on a new cart that they
might bring it from the house of Abinadab which was on the hill; and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab,
were leading the new cart. 4So they brought it with the ark of God from the house of Abinadab,
which was on the hill; and Ahio was walking ahead of the ark. 5Meanwhile, David and all the
house of Israel were celebrating before the Lord with all kinds of instruments
made of fir wood, and with lyres, harps, tambourines, castanets and cymbals.
